headlines.title: Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh signals steady outlook at IMF appearance; avoids committing to next moves
headlines.summary: At the IMF/World Bank meetings, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said he wouldn't prejudge upcoming rate decisions and indicated the Fed's outlook remains largely unchanged since the September rate increase; he also announced a forthcoming field hearing of a Fed productivity/jobs task force in mid-November. Coverage is based on reporting of Warsh's remarks at the IMF event.

evidence.description: AP report summarizing Warsh remarks at IMF; includes direct reporting on his refusal to pre-commit to future rate moves.
evidence.exact_excerpt: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday he won't prejudge what the U.S. central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings in October and December.

evidence.description: Axios coverage noting Warsh's comments and mention of a planned Fed field hearing on productivity and jobs.
evidence.exact_excerpt: Warsh announced that the Fed will hold the first field hearing of its productivity and jobs task force on Nov. 16 in the Bay Area.

headlines.claim_evidence_note: Cited authority cited_authority_unavailable_or_not_inspected; literal excerpt presence is not semantic proof.
headlines.attribution: AP reporting based on Warsh's public remarks at IMF; Axios reporting corroborates and adds the field hearing item.
headlines.what_is_known: Warsh publicly stated he would not pre-commit to future rate actions and described the economy as largely performing as expected since the September rate increase. Axios reports a scheduled Nov. 16 field hearing.
headlines.uncertainty: No Federal Reserve press statement reproducing a full transcript of the IMF remarks was located in the inspected Fed press pages; direct Fed transcript would reduce uncertainty.
headlines.what_cannot_be_concluded: Whether the Fed will change policy at upcoming meetings or the degree of any change — Warsh's remarks are non-committal and do not constitute a policy decision.
headlines.resolution_needed: A Fed press release or full transcript of Warsh's speech/Q&A (if released) would provide primary confirmation of quoted items and the announced field hearing.

headlines.title: Freddie Mac: 30-year fixed mortgage rate holds near 7.40%
headlines.summary: Freddie Mac reported the national 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.40%, unchanged from the prior week — the highest level in nearly three years per their PMMS release.

evidence.description: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) weekly release showing the 30-year fixed average.
evidence.exact_excerpt: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.40% as of October 8, 2026, up from last week when it averaged 7.28%.

evidence.description: AP summary of Freddie Mac's published weekly PMMS noting the 7.4% figure and contextualizing drivers.
evidence.exact_excerpt: The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was unchanged from last week at 7.40%, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday.

headlines.attribution: Freddie Mac (primary data) and AP (independent reporting).
headlines.what_is_known: Freddie Mac's published PMMS lists the 30-year fixed-rate average at 7.40% (week reported as of Oct 8, 2026 on their PMMS page and cited by AP on Oct 15).

headlines.title: Federal Register posting outlines proposed exchange rules for commodity-based crypto trusts
headlines.summary: A Federal Register notice published Oct 7, 2026 (govinfo) details proposed rule language imposing listing and surveillance requirements for crypto commodity-based trusts (example: Bitcoin), including minimum average daily market value and surveillance-sharing expectations.

evidence.description: Federal Register / govinfo PDF of the proposed exchange rule change describing criteria for Commodity-Based Trusts, market-value thresholds and surveillance-sharing.
evidence.exact_excerpt: The proposed rule change would require a Commodity-Based Trust to: (1) meet the generic criteria of a U.S. equities listing exchange... (A) the total global supply of each underlying crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust has an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months; and (B) each crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust underlies a derivatives contract that trades on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement...
